newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 2.21 pct after steep falls.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 2.21 pct after steep falls.

text.p: Thai stocks ended a rollercoaster day on Friday by posting gains of 2.21 percent at the close on bargain-hunting after falling by over 4.53 percent earlier in the day, brokers said.
There was also talk that Far Eastern speculators may have moved in and a government support fund had bought blue chips in banks and finance to shore up the market, they added.

The index smartly recovered in a late rally up 15.42 points to 713.48. At the lunch break the index was down 31.6 points at 666.42 amid heavy selling triggered by a Moody's Investors Service report that said it might cut Thailand's long term debt ratings, brokers said.

"Bargain hunters from Taiwan, Japan and South Korea began buying less than one hour before the market closed. They bought shares mainly in the banking and finance sectors," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
One broker said the SET surged on market rumours that some government agencies had bought blue-chip bank and finance issues. But this could not be confirmed.

"There was no positive news in the market and the buying by foreigners was meant for a pure speculative reasons. Local retail investors must be careful as the foreigners may again dump the market any time," said Thanawat.
Despite the gain in the index, decliners led gainers 183 to 155 while 91 issues unchanged.
Key sectors rose across the board today. The banking sector advanced 1.5 percent and the finance sector gained 0.78 percent.
Siam Commercial Bank topped the active list, falling two baht to 137. Finance One rose 0.75 to 27.50 while TelecomAsia gained two to 46 and Siam Cement advanced four to 664.
